1.explanation:
This minimal React app demonstrates the behavior described in the bug report. It uses:
- carbon-components-react 7.4.1
- carbon-components 10.4.1
- react-router-dom 5.x with a HashRouter and SideNavLink elements

When you shrink your browser width into the small or medium breakpoint, the HeaderMenuButton toggles the SideNav and shows the overlay. In this setup, clicking a SideNavLink updates the Router view but does not collapse the nav, and clicking anywhere on the overlay or header outside the nav also does not collapse it. This reproduces the two issues: 1. SideNav stays open after a link click. 2. Overlay or outside clicks do not close the SideNav. You can inspect or hook into the onClick events to implement a fix (for example, listening for navigation events or overlay clicks to call the expand toggle).
1.bug_scenario:
On a small or medium viewport (when the hamburger menu is shown), clicking the HeaderMenuButton expands the side navigation and displays a gray page overlay. Then:

1. Clicking any SideNavLink (e.g. “Link1” or “Link2”) loads new content but leaves the SideNav expanded (it does not collapse).  
2. Clicking anywhere on the overlay (or on the top bar outside the SideNav) does not close the SideNav — the overlay remains and the SideNav stays open.  

In most apps, you’d expect both clicking a link and clicking the overlay to automatically collapse the side nav.
